<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="prerequisites"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#prerequisites">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer">Prerequisites</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Before configuring Claude Code with Amazon Bedrock, ensure you have:</span>
<ul>
<li>An AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access enabled</li>
<li>Access to desired Claude models (for example, Claude Sonnet 4.6) in Amazon Bedrock</li>
<li>AWS CLI installed and configured (optional - only needed if you don’t have another mechanism for getting credentials)</li>
<li>Appropriate IAM permissions</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">To sign in with your own Amazon Bedrock credentials, follow <a class="link" href="#sign-in-with-bedrock">Sign in with Amazon Bedrock</a> below. To deploy Claude Code across a team, use the <a class="link" href="#set-up-manually">manual setup</a> steps and <a class="link" href="#4-pin-model-versions">pin your model versions</a> before rolling out.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sign-in-with-bedrock"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sign-in-with-bedrock">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Sign in with Bedrock</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">If you have AWS credentials and want to start using Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock, the login wizard walks you through it. You complete the AWS-side prerequisites once per account; the wizard handles the Claude Code side.</span>
<div class="steps ml-3.5 mt-10 mb-6" role="list"><div class="step group/step step-container relative flex items-start pb-5" role="listitem"><div class="absolute w-px h-[calc(100%-2.75rem)] top-11 bg-gray-200/70 dark:bg-white/10" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-line"></div><div class="absolute ml-[-13px] py-2" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-number"><div class="group/step-indicator relative size-7 shrink-0 rounded-full bg-gray-50 dark:bg-white/10 text-xs text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-50 font-semibold flex items-center justify-center"><div class="group-has-[a:focus-visible]/step-indicator:opacity-0">1</div></div></div><div class="w-full overflow-hidden pl-8 pr-px"><p class="mt-2 font-semibold prose dark:prose-invert text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-200" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-title">Enable Anthropic models in your AWS account</p><div class="prose dark:prose-invert" data-component-part="step-content"><span data-as="p">In the <a class="link" href="https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Amazon Bedrock console</a>, open the Model catalog, select an Anthropic model, and submit the use case form. Access is granted immediately after submission. See <a class="link" href="#1-submit-use-case-details">Submit use case details</a> for AWS Organizations and <a class="link" href="#iam-configuration">IAM configuration</a> for the permissions your role needs.</span></div></div></div><div class="step group/step step-container relative flex items-start pb-5" role="listitem"><div class="absolute w-px h-[calc(100%-2.75rem)] top-11 bg-gray-200/70 dark:bg-white/10" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-line"></div><div class="absolute ml-[-13px] py-2" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-number"><div class="group/step-indicator relative size-7 shrink-0 rounded-full bg-gray-50 dark:bg-white/10 text-xs text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-50 font-semibold flex items-center justify-center"><div class="group-has-[a:focus-visible]/step-indicator:opacity-0">2</div></div></div><div class="w-full overflow-hidden pl-8 pr-px"><p class="mt-2 font-semibold prose dark:prose-invert text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-200" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-title">Start Claude Code and choose Amazon Bedrock</p><div class="prose dark:prose-invert" data-component-part="step-content"><span data-as="p">Run <code>claude</code>. At the login prompt, select <strong>3rd-party platform</strong>, then <strong>Amazon Bedrock</strong>. If you’re already signed in and see the chat prompt instead, run <code>/setup-bedrock</code> to open the wizard. Until <code>CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1</code> is set, Claude Code <a class="link" href="/docs/en/commands#how-the-command-menu-matches-what-you-type">hides the command from the command menu</a>; type it in full.</span></div></div></div><div class="step group/step step-container relative flex items-start pb-5" role="listitem"><div class='absolute w-px h-[calc(100%-2.75rem)] top-11 bg-transparent bg-linear-to-b from-gray-200 dark:from-white/10 via-80% to-transparent group-has-[[data-component-part="step-content"]:empty]/step:hidden' contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-line"></div><div class="absolute ml-[-13px] py-2" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-number"><div class="group/step-indicator relative size-7 shrink-0 rounded-full bg-gray-50 dark:bg-white/10 text-xs text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-50 font-semibold flex items-center justify-center"><div class="group-has-[a:focus-visible]/step-indicator:opacity-0">3</div></div></div><div class="w-full overflow-hidden pl-8 pr-px"><p class="mt-2 font-semibold prose dark:prose-invert text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-200" contenteditable="false" data-component-part="step-title">Follow the wizard prompts</p><div class="prose dark:prose-invert" data-component-part="step-content"><span data-as="p">Choose how you authenticate to AWS: an AWS profile detected from your <code>~/.aws</code> directory, an Amazon Bedrock API key, an access key and secret, or credentials already in your environment. The wizard asks for your region, verifies which Claude models your account can invoke, and lets you pin them. It saves the result to the <code>env</code> block of your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">user settings file</a>, so you don’t need to export environment variables yourself.</span></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">After you’ve signed in, run <code>/setup-bedrock</code> any time to reopen the wizard and change your credentials, region, or model pins. The model pin step starts from your currently pinned models. The wizard writes to <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>, or to <code>$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json</code> when <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars#variables"><code>CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR</code></a> is set.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="set-up-manually"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#set-up-manually">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Set up manually</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">To configure Amazon Bedrock through environment variables instead of the wizard, for example in CI or a scripted enterprise rollout, follow the steps below.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="1-submit-use-case-details"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#1-submit-use-case-details">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">1. Submit use case details</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Before you invoke an Anthropic model for the first time, submit use case details. You do this once per AWS account.</span>
<ol>
<li>Ensure you have the right IAM permissions described below</li>
<li>Navigate to the <a class="link" href="https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Amazon Bedrock console</a></li>
<li>Select an Anthropic model from the <strong>Model catalog</strong></li>
<li>Complete the use case form. Access is granted immediately after submission.</li>
</ol>
<span data-as="p">If you use AWS Organizations, you can submit the form once from the management account using the <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_PutUseCaseForModelAccess.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank"><code>PutUseCaseForModelAccess</code> API</a>. This call requires the <code>bedrock:PutUseCaseForModelAccess</code> IAM permission. Approval extends to child accounts automatically.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="2-configure-aws-credentials"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#2-configure-aws-credentials">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">2. Configure AWS credentials</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code uses the default AWS SDK credential chain. Set up your credentials using one of these methods:</span>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code requests role credentials from the IAM Identity Center region named by the profile’s <code>sso_region</code>, which doesn’t need to match the region you run Amazon Bedrock in. In v2.1.207, the Amazon Bedrock region overrode <code>sso_region</code>, so a profile whose IAM Identity Center instance is in a different region failed to authenticate with a <code>Session token not found or invalid</code> error.</span>

<span data-as="p">Amazon Bedrock API keys provide a simpler authentication method without needing full AWS credentials. <a class="link" href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/accelerate-ai-development-with-amazon-bedrock-api-keys/" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Learn more about Amazon Bedrock API keys</a>.</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="credential-caching-and-resolution-timeout"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#credential-caching-and-resolution-timeout">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Credential caching and resolution timeout</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code resolves the AWS default credential provider chain once and keeps the resolved credentials in memory. It reuses them until five minutes before they expire, or for one hour when they carry no expiration, so an SSO-backed profile requests credentials from IAM Identity Center about once per credential lifetime. A credential error from the API clears the cache, and the retry resolves fresh credentials. Requires Claude Code v2.1.207 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">The cache covers every credential option above except an Amazon Bedrock API key, which doesn’t use the provider chain. To resolve the chain on every request instead, set <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_AWS_CRED_CACHE=1</code></a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Each resolve of the chain times out after 60 seconds. If a step in the chain stalls, for example a <code>credential_process</code> helper that waits for input it can’t receive, the request fails with <a class="link" href="/docs/en/errors#aws-default-chain-credential-resolve-timed-out"><code>AWS default-chain credential resolve timed out</code></a>. If your chain runs an interactive sign-in that legitimately needs longer, such as browser-based SSO with MFA through a wrapper like <code>aws-vault</code>, raise the limit in milliseconds with <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_AWS_CHAIN_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS</code></a>. Before v2.1.207, a stalled credential resolution left the request waiting indefinitely.</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="advanced-credential-configuration"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#advanced-credential-configuration">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Advanced credential configuration</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code supports automatic credential refresh for AWS SSO and corporate identity providers. Add these settings to your Claude Code settings file (see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">Settings</a> for file locations).</span>
<span data-as="p">These two settings have different trigger conditions:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>awsAuthRefresh</code></strong>: runs only when Claude Code detects that your AWS credentials are expired, either locally based on their timestamp or when the API returns a credential error, then retries the request with refreshed credentials.</li>
<li><strong><code>awsCredentialExport</code></strong>: runs at session start and on each credential reload, even when the credentials in your AWS default credential provider chain are still valid. Use this when your Amazon Bedrock account requires cross-account credentials that differ from the ones the default provider chain would resolve.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Before running the <code>awsAuthRefresh</code> command, Claude Code makes an STS <code>GetCallerIdentity</code> call to confirm that your credentials are actually expired, and skips the command when they still work. Claude Code sends this check through your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/network-config#proxy-configuration">proxy configuration</a>, honoring <code>HTTPS_PROXY</code> and <code>NO_PROXY</code>. Before v2.1.239, Claude Code sent this check directly and hung at startup on networks that only allow egress through a proxy.</span>

<h5>Configuration settings explained</h5>
<span data-as="p"><strong><code>awsAuthRefresh</code></strong>: Use this for commands that modify the <code>.aws</code> directory, such as updating credentials, SSO cache, or config files. The command’s output is displayed to the user, but interactive input isn’t supported. This works well for browser-based SSO flows where the CLI displays a URL or code and you complete authentication in the browser.</span>
<span data-as="p"><strong><code>awsCredentialExport</code></strong>: Only use this if you can’t modify <code>.aws</code> and must directly return credentials. Output is captured silently and not shown to the user. The command must output JSON in this format:</span>
<div class="code-block mt-5 mb-8 not-prose rounded-2xl relative group min-w-0 print:print-color-exact text-gray-950 dark:text-gray-50 codeblock-light border border-gray-950/10 dark:border-white/10 <span data-as="p">As of Claude Code v2.1.181, the flat output from <code>aws configure export-credentials --format process</code> is also accepted, with the same keys at the top level instead of nested under <code>Credentials</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p"><code>Expiration</code> is optional. As of Claude Code v2.1.176, when the command returns a valid ISO 8601 <code>Expiration</code>, Claude Code caches the credentials until five minutes before that time. Without it, or on earlier versions, credentials are cached for one hour.</span>
<span data-as="p">When you configure <code>awsCredentialExport</code> without <code>awsAuthRefresh</code>, Claude Code uses the exported credentials directly and doesn’t re-resolve the AWS default credential provider chain at startup. Requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later.</span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#569CD6">export</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE"> AWS_REGION</span><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">=</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">us-east-1</span><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955">  # optional if your AWS profile already sets a region</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># Optional: Override the AWS region for the small/fast model (Bedrock and Mantle).</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># On Bedrock, has no effect without ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># or the deprecated ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL set.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#569CD6">export</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE"> ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL_AWS_REGION</span><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">=</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">us-west-2</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># Optional: Override the Bedrock endpoint URL for custom endpoints or gateways</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># export ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL=https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com</span></span>

<span data-as="p">When enabling Amazon Bedrock for Claude Code, keep the following in mind:</span>
<ul>
<li>
<span data-as="p">As of v2.1.172, you only need to set <code>AWS_REGION</code> to override your AWS profile’s region or when your profile has no region. Claude Code resolves the region in this order:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>AWS_REGION</code></li>
<li><code>AWS_DEFAULT_REGION</code></li>
<li>the <code>region</code> set on your active AWS profile, read from the AWS shared credentials file first and then the shared config file, matching AWS SDK precedence</li>
<li><code>us-east-1</code></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">If a value from any of these sources isn’t shaped like a region name, Claude Code treats it as unset and continues down the order. For example, Claude Code treats a value containing a slash, dot, or space as unset.</span>
<span data-as="p">The active profile is <code>AWS_PROFILE</code> if set, otherwise <code>default</code>. Set <code>AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE</code> or <code>AWS_CONFIG_FILE</code> to point at non-default file paths.</span>
<span data-as="p">Run <code>/status</code> to see the resolved region. When the region came from your AWS config files or the default fallback, Claude Code also notes the source in the <code>/status</code> output. On v2.1.171 and earlier, Claude Code doesn’t read the AWS config files, so set <code>AWS_REGION</code> explicitly.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p">When using Amazon Bedrock, the <code>/logout</code> command is unavailable since authentication is handled through AWS credentials.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p">The WebSearch tool is not available on Amazon Bedrock. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/tools-reference#websearch-tool-behavior">WebSearch tool behavior</a>.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p">You can use settings files for environment variables like <code>AWS_PROFILE</code> that you don’t want to leak to other processes. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">Settings</a> for more information.</span>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="4-pin-model-versions"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#4-pin-model-versions">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">4. Pin model versions</span></h3>
<div aria-label="Warning" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-yellow-200 bg-yellow-50 dark:border-yellow-900 dark:bg-yellow-600/20 [&amp;_[data-component-part='callout-icon']]:mt-px" data-callout-type="warning" role="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="flex-none size-5 text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M 9 6.75 v 1.5 m 0 3 h 0.0075 m -5.2035 3 h 10.392 c 1.155 0 1.8765 -1.2503 1.299 -2.25 L 10.299 3 c -0.5775 -0.9997 -2.0205 -0.9997 -2.598 0 L 2.505 12 c -0.5775 0.9997 0.144 2.25 1.299 2.25 z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">Pin specific model versions when deploying to multiple users. Without pinning, model aliases such as <code>sonnet</code> and <code>opus</code> resolve to Claude Code’s built-in default for Amazon Bedrock, which can lag the newest release and may not yet be available in your account. Claude Code <a class="link" href="#startup-model-checks">falls back</a> to an earlier or lower-tier model at startup when the default is unavailable, but pinning lets you control when your users move to a new model.</span></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Set these environment variables to specific Amazon Bedrock model IDs.</span>
<span data-as="p">Without <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL</code>, the <code>opus</code> alias on Amazon Bedrock resolves to Opus 5, and without <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL</code>, the <code>sonnet</code> alias resolves to Sonnet 4.5. This example pins each alias to a specific version:</span>

<span data-as="p">These IDs use the <code>us.</code> cross-region inference profile prefix. If you use a different region prefix or application inference profiles, adjust accordingly. In AWS GovCloud regions, use the <code>us-gov.</code> prefix.</span>
<span data-as="p">To keep the built-in default models and change only their preferred prefix, set <a class="link" href="#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes"><code>ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX</code></a> instead of pinning. The difference shows in what the <code>opus</code> alias resolves to:</span>
<!-- --><div class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px"><div aria-label="Scrollable table" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" data-id="base-ui-_R_fcllktbsnlhjiuasnpfiutb_-viewport" role="region" style="overflow:scroll" tabindex="-1"><div class="flex" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px] [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left">You set</th><th style="text-align:left">The <code>opus</code> alias resolves to</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL='us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8'</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8</code>, the exact ID you pinned</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX=eu</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>eu.anthropic.claude-opus-5</code>, the built-in default with your preferred prefix</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">For current and legacy model IDs, see <a class="link" href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Models overview</a>. For the full list of pinning environment variables, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#pin-models-for-third-party-deployments">Model configuration</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code uses these default models when no pinning variables are set:</span>
<!-- --><div class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px"><div aria-label="Scrollable table" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" data-id="base-ui-_R_g4llktbsnlhjiuasnpfiutb_-viewport" role="region" style="overflow:scroll" tabindex="-1"><div class="flex" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px] [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left">Model type</th><th style="text-align:left">Default model</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left">Primary model</td><td style="text-align:left">Opus 5, for example <code>us.anthropic.claude-opus-5</code> in a <code>us-*</code> region</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Small/fast model</td><td style="text-align:left">Sonnet 4.5, for example <code>us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0</code> in a <code>us-*</code> region</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Background tasks such as session title generation use the small/fast model, normally a Haiku-class model. On Amazon Bedrock, Claude Code uses the default Sonnet model for background tasks because Haiku may not be enabled in every account or region. Two selections change which model carries them:</span>
<ul>
<li>When you select a primary model with <code>--model</code>, <code>ANTHROPIC_MODEL</code>, or the <code>model</code> setting, background tasks use that model. When Claude Code starts the session on the model you set with <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#set-a-default-model-for-new-sessions"><code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL</code></a>, background tasks use that model too. Setting <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL</code> without <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL</code> also counts as a selection, because the built-in Sonnet model may not be enabled in an account that steers its own Opus.</li>
<li>To use Haiku for background tasks, set <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL</code> to a model ID that is available in your account.</li>
</ul>
<div aria-label="Warning" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-yellow-200 bg-yellow-50 dark:border-yellow-900 dark:bg-yellow-600/20 [&amp;_[data-component-part='callout-icon']]:mt-px" data-callout-type="warning" role="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="flex-none size-5 text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M 9 6.75 v 1.5 m 0 3 h 0.0075 m -5.2035 3 h 10.392 c 1.155 0 1.8765 -1.2503 1.299 -2.25 L 10.299 3 c -0.5775 -0.9997 -2.0205 -0.9997 -2.598 0 L 2.505 12 c -0.5775 0.9997 0.144 2.25 1.299 2.25 z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">Opus models have a higher per-token price than Sonnet models, so a deployment that doesn’t pin a primary model is billed at the Opus rate once it updates to v2.1.207 or later. To keep Sonnet 4.5 as the primary model, set <code>ANTHROPIC_MODEL</code> to its full model ID. A deployment that steers the default with <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL</code> and doesn’t set <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL</code> keeps its steered Sonnet model as the default.</span></div></div>
<span data-as="p">On v2.1.207 through v2.1.218, the primary model on Amazon Bedrock defaulted to Opus 4.8 and the <code>opus</code> alias resolved to Opus 4.8. Before v2.1.207, the primary model defaulted to Sonnet 4.5, the <code>opus</code> alias resolved to Opus 4.6, and background tasks always used the primary model.</span>
<span data-as="p">To customize models further, use one of these methods:</span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># Optional: Request 1-hour prompt cache TTL instead of the 5-minute default</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># export ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1</span></span>
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div aria-hidden="true" class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">The 1-hour cache TTL is billed at a higher rate than the 5-minute default. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime">cache lifetime</a>. To set different TTLs for your main conversation and for the requests Claude Code makes outside it, <a class="link" href="/docs/en/prompt-caching#choose-the-ttl-yourself">choose the TTL yourself</a>.</span>
<div aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note" role="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path clip-rule="evenodd" d="M 9 1.6714 C 13.0371 1.6714 16.3286 4.9629 16.3286 9 C 16.3286 13.0371 13.0371 16.3286 9 16.3286 C 7.0574 16.3252 5.1953 15.552 3.8217 14.1783 C 2.448 12.8047 1.6748 10.9426 1.6714 9 C 1.6714 4.9629 4.9629 1.6714 9 1.6714 Z M 9 0 C 4.0371 0 0 4.0371 0 9 C 0 13.9629 4.0371 18 9 18 C 13.9629 18 18 13.9629 18 9 C 18 4.0371 13.9629 0 9 0 Z M 10.2857 3.8571 H 7.7143 V 10.2857 H 10.2857 V 3.8571 Z M 10.2857 11.5714 H 7.7143 V 14.1429 H 10.2857 V 11.5714 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-rule="evenodd" stroke="none"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! If cache token counts stay at zero, check <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html#prompt-caching-models" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">supported models, regions, and limits</a> in the Amazon Bedrock documentation.</div></div>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Map each model version to an inference profile</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">The <code>ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL</code> environment variables configure one inference profile per model family. If your organization needs to expose several versions of the same family in the <code>/model</code> picker, each routed to its own application inference profile ARN, use the <code>modelOverrides</code> setting in your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings#where-settings-live">settings file</a> instead.</span>
<span data-as="p">This example maps four Opus versions to distinct ARNs so users can switch between them without bypassing your organization’s inference profiles:</span>

<span data-as="p">When a user selects one of these versions in <code>/model</code>, Claude Code calls Amazon Bedrock with the mapped ARN. The same mapping applies when you pass the Anthropic model ID directly through <code>--model</code> or <code>ANTHROPIC_MODEL</code>. Versions without an override fall back to the built-in Amazon Bedrock model ID or any matching inference profile discovered at startup. Before v2.1.200, <code>--model</code> and <code>ANTHROPIC_MODEL</code> values reached Amazon Bedrock as-is without going through the override map. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#override-model-ids-per-version">Override model IDs per version</a> for details on how overrides interact with <code>availableModels</code> and other model settings.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="startup-model-checks"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#startup-model-checks">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Startup model checks</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">When Claude Code starts with Amazon Bedrock configured, it verifies that the models it intends to use are accessible in your account.</span>
<span data-as="p">If you have pinned a model version that is older than the current Claude Code default, and your account can invoke the newer version, Claude Code prompts you to update the pin. Accepting writes the new model ID to your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">user settings file</a> and restarts Claude Code. Declining is remembered until the next default version change. Pins that point to an <a class="link" href="#map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile">application inference profile ARN</a> are skipped, since those are managed by your administrator.</span>
<span data-as="p">If you have not pinned a model and the current default is unavailable in your account, Claude Code falls back for the current session and shows a notice. It tries earlier versions of the default model first and, when the default is an Opus model and no Opus version is available, falls back to the default Sonnet model. The fallback is not persisted. Enable the newer model in your Amazon Bedrock account or <a class="link" href="#4-pin-model-versions">pin a version</a> to make the choice permanent.</span>
<span data-as="p">When you start the session on a specific Sonnet or Opus version, for example with <code>--model</code>, <code>ANTHROPIC_MODEL</code>, or the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-reference#model"><code>model</code> setting</a>, that version acts as the session’s pinned default for the matching <code>sonnet</code> or <code>opus</code> alias. Claude Code skips the availability check for the built-in default your model replaces and starts on the model you configured, with no fallback notice.</span>
<span data-as="p">Model aliases such as <code>opus</code> don’t act as pins, and neither does a model ID Claude Code doesn’t recognize, such as an application inference profile ARN.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#cross-region-inference-profile-prefixes">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Cross-region inference profile prefixes</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">On the Amazon Bedrock <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_InvokeModelWithResponseStream.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Invoke API</a>, Claude Code resolves its built-in default models to <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-profiles-support.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">cross-region inference profile</a> IDs; to route model versions through your own inference profiles instead, see <a class="link" href="#map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile">Map each model version to an inference profile</a>. This table shows the prefix Claude Code prefers for each resolved AWS region:</span>
<!-- --><div class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px"><div aria-label="Scrollable table" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" data-id="base-ui-_R_lkllktbsnlhjiuasnpfiutb_-viewport" role="region" style="overflow:scroll" tabindex="-1"><div class="flex" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px] [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left">AWS region</th><th style="text-align:left">Prefix</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>us-gov-*</code> (AWS GovCloud)</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>us-gov.</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>us-*</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>us.</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>eu-*</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>eu.</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>ap-*</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>apac.</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">All other regions</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>global.</code></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Set <code>ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX</code> to choose the prefix Claude Code tries first; when Claude Code can check profile availability and finds no matching profile for a model, it falls back as described in the resolution order below. Valid values are <code>us</code>, <code>eu</code>, <code>apac</code>, <code>jp</code>, <code>au</code>, and <code>global</code>. For example, set it to <code>global</code> when your account has <code>global.</code> profiles enabled but Claude Code would derive a geography-specific one from your AWS region. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">This example routes the default models through <code>global.</code> profiles:</span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># In a us-* region, the primary model now resolves to</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6E7781;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"># global.anthropic.claude-opus-5 instead of us.anthropic.claude-opus-5</span></span>
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div aria-hidden="true" class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">The preferred prefix is a preference, not a guarantee, whether it comes from your region or from the variable. How Claude Code applies it depends on whether it can check profile availability in your account:</span>
<ul>
<li>When Claude Code can <a class="link" href="#iam-configuration">list the inference profiles</a> in your account, it resolves each model in this order:<!-- -->
<ol>
<li>The profile with your preferred prefix.</li>
<li>Any matching profile, for a model that has no profile with that prefix.</li>
<li>The built-in model ID with your preferred prefix, for a model that has no matching profile at all. Claude Code applies this ID without checking availability at this step; the <a class="link" href="#startup-model-checks">startup model checks</a> still cover the session’s default models.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>When profile discovery is unavailable, Claude Code applies the prefix without checking availability. If your account doesn’t have inference profiles with that prefix enabled, requests fail with a 400 error.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code doesn’t rewrite Amazon Bedrock inference profile IDs or ARNs you configure yourself, or <a class="link" href="#map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile"><code>modelOverrides</code></a> values; Anthropic-format model IDs resolve through <a class="link" href="#map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile">the same mapping as the <code>/model</code> picker</a>. Claude Code also ignores the variable in two cases:</span>
<ul>
<li>In AWS GovCloud regions, Claude Code always uses <code>us-gov.</code>, the only prefix that routes within the GovCloud partition.</li>
<li>When you set a value that isn’t one of the valid values, Claude Code falls back to the region-derived preferred prefix.</li>
</ul>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">      "Condition"</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: {</span></span>

<span data-as="p">For more restrictive permissions, you can limit the Resource to specific inference profile ARNs.</span>
<span data-as="p"><code>bedrock:GetInferenceProfile</code> lets Claude Code resolve an <a class="link" href="#map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile">application inference profile ARN</a> to its backing foundation model, which is used to select the correct request shape for that model.</span>
<span data-as="p">If the token is missing this permission, Claude Code recovers automatically by retrying once with the alternate shape, so requests still succeed but each new model adds an extra round-trip. Granting the permission avoids the retry. This applies most often to <code>AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK</code> deployments, where the token’s policy is typically narrower than a full IAM role.</span>
<span data-as="p">For details, see <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-iam.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Amazon Bedrock IAM documentation</a>.</span>

<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="1m-token-context-window"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#1m-token-context-window">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">1M token context window</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 support the <a class="link" href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows#context-window-sizes-by-model" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">1M token context window</a> on Amazon Bedrock. Sonnet 5 always runs with the 1M window on both the Invoke API and the <a class="link" href="#use-the-mantle-endpoint">Mantle endpoint</a>, with no <code>[1m]</code> variant to select. For the other models on the Invoke API, Claude Code automatically enables the extended context window when you select a 1M model variant.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <a class="link" href="#sign-in-with-bedrock">setup wizard</a> offers a 1M context option when it pins models. To enable it for a manually pinned model instead, append <code>[1m]</code> to the model ID. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#pin-models-for-third-party-deployments">Pin models for third-party deployments</a> for details.</span>

Reserved capacity uses a <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prov-throughput.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">provisioned throughput</a> ARN as the model ID instead of this setting.</span>

<span data-as="p"><a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Amazon Bedrock Guardrails</a> let you implement content filtering for Claude Code. <h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="use-the-mantle-endpoint"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#use-the-mantle-endpoint">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Use the Mantle endpoint</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API. It uses the same AWS credentials, IAM permissions, and <code>awsAuthRefresh</code> configuration described earlier on this page.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="enable-mantle"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#enable-mantle">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Enable Mantle</span></h3>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code constructs the endpoint URL from the AWS region. As of v2.1.172, the region is resolved with the same precedence as <a class="link" href="#3-configure-claude-code">Amazon Bedrock above</a>; earlier versions use <code>AWS_REGION</code> only. To override the URL for a custom endpoint or gateway, set <code>ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Run <code>/status</code> inside Claude Code to confirm. The provider line shows <code>Amazon Bedrock (Mantle)</code> when Mantle is active.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="select-a-mantle-model"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#select-a-mantle-model">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Select a Mantle model</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Mantle uses model IDs prefixed with <code>anthropic.</code> and without a version suffix, for example <code>anthropic.claude-sonnet-5</code> or <code>anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5</code>. The models available to your account depend on what your organization has been granted; additional model IDs are listed in your onboarding materials from AWS. Contact your AWS account team to request access to allowlisted models.</span>
<span data-as="p">Set the model with the <code>--model</code> flag or with <code>/model</code> inside Claude Code:</span>

<span data-as="p">The models available to you on Mantle may not include every model you use today. Setting both <code>CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK</code> and <code>CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE</code> lets Claude Code call both endpoints from the same session. Model IDs that match the Mantle format are routed to Mantle, and all other model IDs go to the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API.</span>

<span data-as="p">To surface a Mantle model in the <code>/model</code> picker, list its ID in <code>availableModels</code> in your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">settings file</a>. This setting also restricts the picker to the listed entries. Listing <code>anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5</code> removes the bare <code>haiku</code> alias from the picker, so also list version prefixes or full IDs for the versions you want to keep selectable. The Mantle ID and the <code>haiku</code> alias resolve to the same model family, so the merge keeps only the more specific entry. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#merge-behavior">Merge behavior</a>:</span>

<span data-as="p">Entries with the <code>anthropic.</code> prefix are added as custom picker options and routed to Mantle. Replace <code>anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5</code> with the model ID your account has been granted. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#restrict-model-selection">Restrict model selection</a> for how <code>availableModels</code> interacts with other model settings.</span>
<span data-as="p">When both providers are active, <code>/status</code> shows <code>Amazon Bedrock + Amazon Bedrock (Mantle)</code>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="route-mantle-through-a-gateway"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#route-mantle-through-a-gateway">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Route Mantle through a gateway</span></h3>
